analytics.title: Orbit Usage
analytics.hoursByProjectInfo: The total estimates the combined working time (Orbit + you), not raw clock time. Orbit's generation time always counts. Your breaks enter with an inactivity margin: up to 30 min count in full (reading, testing or reviewing); 30–60 min count in full if you return with a detailed message; 1–1.5 h count only half, and only with a very long message. Longer breaks — or ones without a message that shows work — don't count.

howto.title: Modes and Tools
howto.description: Orbit offers several modes that change the agent's behavior. Turn them on before sending your message and combine them for more complex tasks.

recommended.title: Recommended Combinations
recommended.description: Some modes work better together. Here are tested combinations:

tip.title: Tip
tip.text: All modes and their settings are available in the message input. Use the toggles below the input to turn them on/off quickly, or click the "+" button to access Subagents, Orchestra, and Loop with their advanced settings.

modes.label: Research
modes.description: Searches and reads web pages via HTTP.
modes.detail: Adds the websearch and webfetch tools to the agent. Fast and efficient for looking up documentation, APIs, and public information. Doesn't run JavaScript — ideal for static content.

modes.label: Browser
modes.description: Navigates pages like a real browser.
modes.detail: Opens the right panel with a full browser. Runs JavaScript, ideal for SPAs, forms, and dynamic pages. The agent can navigate, click, fill fields, and take screenshots.

modes.label: Thinking
modes.detail: Enables the model's reasoning/thinking mode (when supported). The model "thinks" before answering, resulting in deeper, better-grounded replies. Uses more tokens and time.

modes.label: Simple
modes.detail: Removes advanced formatting, citations, and tool blocks from the response. Useful when you just want the essential content, no frills.

modes.label: Memory (Brain)
modes.description: Orbit remembers facts and preferences across conversations.
modes.detail: Adds the memory_save/search/link/open/graph tools. Orbit can save facts, preferences, and decisions and automatically retrieve them in future conversations. Turn it off per chat if you prefer a context-free interaction.

modes.label: Subagents
modes.description: Ephemeral background workers for parallel tasks.
modes.detail: Adds the subagent tool to the agent. When it spots independent subtasks, it can delegate them to ephemeral workers running in the background with the configured model. Those workers are discarded when the task ends — they never appear in the sidebar. In Orchestra mode this toggle is also what lets the orchestrator delegate research while planning: without it, it investigates the project itself by reading files.

modes.label: Orchestra
modes.description: Plans and splits work across persistent workers — when the request calls for it.
modes.detail: The orchestrator first decides what the message actually is: a simple question it answers on the spot (and may offer "want me to implement this?"), an ambiguity that would change the split it asks about, and only real work becomes a plan. When planning, it reads the project itself and registers subtasks with create_task, proposing the plan for your approval. Each approved task becomes a persistent child session, always in code mode in the working folder, running in parallel with the worker model. It picks each worker’s modes based on what that task needs, within what you enabled in this conversation. At the end it synthesises everything and reviews: if something came out wrong, it sends another round to the worker responsible, inside that worker’s own chat. In later messages it still sees this conversation’s workers (from any plan): it reads what each one did, sees what you typed directly in a worker, and can continue a worker’s conversation instead of creating a new one.

modes.label: Loop
modes.description: The agent reviews and iterates until the task is complete.
modes.detail: After each answer the result is critically reviewed. If the goal wasn’t met, the agent keeps going on its own in a new iteration, with the gap spelled out. The only setting is max iterations (in the gear) — and it is a ceiling, not a target: the loop stops as soon as the review says it is done. In Orchestra mode that same number becomes the total review rounds across all workers.

modes.label: Plan Mode
modes.description: Read-only — produces a plan without editing files.
modes.detail: Blocks write tools (write, edit, bash). The agent only reads the code and produces a detailed implementation plan. Useful for review and planning before making changes.

modes.label: Permissions
modes.description: Security control over the agent's actions.
modes.detail: Three levels: Ask (asks before each critical action), Approve (shows a summary for approval), Full (executes automatically). Configurable in the Preferences modal or directly in the input.

modes.label: Vision
modes.description: Delegates vision to a dedicated model.
modes.detail: With the mode on, images (screenshots and attachments) are described by a configured vision model and only the text description enters the agent's context — never the raw image. Beneficial even for models with native vision: in long conversations, the image isn't reloaded into the context every turn, saving tokens and keeping the context lean.

combos.label: Deep research
combos.description: Turn on Research + Browser + Thinking together. The agent searches, navigates complex pages, and reasons deeply about what it found. Ideal for investigating technical topics, comparing documentation, or doing competitive analysis.

combos.label: Automatic refinement
combos.description: Loop + Thinking: the agent reviews its own result with extended reasoning, spotting gaps and refining until the goal is achieved. Great for generating robust code, thorough tests, or detailed documentation.

combos.label: Orchestration with review
combos.description: Orchestra + Loop: without Loop, the orchestrator gets 2 review rounds after synthesis — enough to fix the obvious mistake. With Loop on, the budget becomes the max iterations you configured (default 5). These are TOTAL rounds, not per worker: the orchestrator decides where to spend them, since it is the only one seeing the whole picture.

combos.label: Workers on multiple fronts
combos.description: Orchestra + Subagents: unlocks delegation at both levels. While planning, the orchestrator may call subagents to research before splitting (without the toggle it reads the project itself). And it can hand a worker its own subagents when a task is too broad for one.

combos.label: Orchestra + Subagents + Loop
combos.description: Orchestra + Subagents + Loop: the most autonomous setup — and the most expensive. Delegated research while planning, workers that can split themselves further, and Loop’s larger review budget. Worth it for genuinely large jobs; check the estimated cost on the plan card before approving.

combos.label: Careful planning
combos.description: Plan Mode + Thinking + Research: before any change, the agent researches documentation, reasons deeply, and produces a detailed implementation plan without modifying files. Approve the plan, then execute it with the normal tools.

combos.label: Safe coding
combos.description: Ask permission + Loop: on each loop iteration, the agent can ask for permission before sensitive actions (editing files, running commands). Safe for reviewing third-party code or making changes in production.

esteira.exclusaoTaskDescricaoWorktree: This action cannot be undone — the task, its notes and its worktree will be deleted, along with anything not committed. The {{branch}} branch stays in the repository.
esteira.worktreePorTask: Isolate each task in a worktree
esteira.worktreePorTaskDica: Each task works on its own branch and copy, so several can run at once without touching each other. Starts from the current branch (uncommitted changes are left out) and applies to tasks that haven't started yet.
esteira.dependenciasVinculadas: node_modules linked to the main checkout
esteira.subtitulo: Pipelines that run tasks phase by phase, without chats
esteira.faseDescricaoDica: One line — shown in the pipeline list
esteira.faseTipoDica: Defines what the phase does (and what it leaves to the next ones), regardless of its name
esteira.fasePromptDica: Instructions for the agent in this phase, including what it must record in the note.
esteira.salvarComoNovaFase: Create a new phase and save
esteira.seguePadrao: Follows the pipeline's default model. Pick another to give this phase its own.
esteira.excluirFaseConfirmar: "{{nome}}" will no longer appear in "Add phase". Pipelines that already use it are unchanged.
esteira.devolverDica: The task goes back through the pipeline as round {{rodada}}, building on what it already did. Your comment takes priority over the original description.
esteira.devolverPlaceholder: E.g.: The shipping calculation is wrong — it must use dimensional weight. And the button should be disabled while it calculates.
esteira.devolverDependentes_one: {{titulos}} depends on this task and already ran against the previous version.
esteira.devolverDependentes_other: {{count}} tasks depend on this one and already ran against the previous version: {{titulos}}.
esteira.rodadaTitulo: Round {{rodada}}: the task was sent back for review
esteira.retomarInstrucaoDica: The “{{fase}}” phase runs again following your instruction. Later phases receive it too, as context.
esteira.retomarInstrucaoPlaceholder: E.g.: Tests run with npm run test:unit, not npm test. Or: don't touch the database schema, only the API.
esteira.naoRodouNaRodada: This phase did not run in this round: it restarted at a later phase. Its work is in the previous round.

desenvolvimento.descricao: Implements the task following the project's conventions

validacao.descricao: Validates the implementation: build, tests and diff review

seguranca.descricao: Audit of dependencies, secrets and permissions

esteira.taskDescricaoDica: The full brief the phases receive — the task runs without a chat, so what is not here never reaches the agent.
esteira.taskDependenciasDica: This task only starts after the selected ones are done.
esteira.semTasksParaDependencia: No other task in this pipeline yet
esteira.commitPromptDica: Prompt used by the agent that writes the final commit message. It receives the task, the notes from every phase and the changed files — exactly the same context a phase gets. Empty uses the default: follow the user's commit preferences from memory, falling back to Conventional Commits (header + body of summarized topics).
esteira.commitPromptVazio: Empty = default prompt (memory preferences → Conventional Commits).

rotinas.subtitulo: Sessions that come back on their own: the agent runs the same prompt on schedule.

criar.descreverDica: Describe it in plain words. The model turns it into a title, prompt, schedule and modes — you review everything in the next step.
criar.placeholder:
E.g.: every day at 9am, review yesterday's commits in this repository and write a summary of what changed, with any risks you find.

Or: every Monday, analyze the project and create improvement tasks in pipeline mode (Orbit's esteira board).
criar.semModelo: Pick a model to generate the routine.
criar.placeholderChat: E.g.: every day at 8am, put together a morning briefing with the day's tech news and a summary of my recent memories.
criar.modoChatDica: Chat mode: the routine runs with no working folders — just the conversation and the chat tools.

revisar.subtitulo: The agent suggested it — confirm or adjust before creating.
revisar.campoPromptDica: This is what the agent receives on every run. It must be self-contained: there is nobody to answer questions.
revisar.modosDica: The agent suggested these based on the work described. Toggle them freely.
revisar.pastasDica: Chosen in this step — the routine always runs in them.
revisar.semPastas: No folder open. Open a folder in code mode before creating the routine.

loop.descricao: The agent reviews its own work and iterates until done.

subagents.descricao: Can delegate parallel investigations to ephemeral workers.

orchestrate.descricao: Splits into a task plan and workers. Implies loop and subagents.

brain.descricao: Persistent memory — this is what makes the routine remember earlier runs.

browser.descricao: Opens and inspects pages in the panel browser.

plan.descricao: Plans only, never executes. The routine waits for approval.

modos.permissaoAviso: The routine fires on its own: on "Ask" it stops at the first sensitive action and waits for you to answer in the run's session.

search.descricao: In-depth web research with search tools.

vision.descricao: Images and screenshots are described by the configured vision model.

lista.vazioSubtitulo: A routine is a session that comes back on its own — a daily report, a weekly sweep, a check after every deploy.
lista.excluirDescricao: "{{titulo}}" and ALL the sessions it produced will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
lista.vazioSubtituloChat: A chat routine is a session that comes back on its own — a daily briefing, a memory digest, a news check.

rotinas.subtituloChat: Chat sessions that come back on their own — no working folders, just conversation and the chat tools.

conversation.emptyDescription: Start a conversation to see messages here

documents.saveFailed: The change could not be saved.
documents.externalChange: The agent rewrote this document while you were editing. Nothing was saved over it — choose which version stays.
documents.useAsSource: Use as a source in this conversation
documents.isSource: Already a source in this conversation

sources.title: Sources
sources.sharedHint: Drop documents here to talk to them from any conversation in this folder.
sources.ownHint: Whatever you attach in the chat shows up here, and stays in this conversation.
sources.noFolderHint: This conversation is not in a folder. Move it into a sidebar folder to share sources across conversations.
sources.textTitlePlaceholder: Title (e.g. Minutes of the March 12 meeting)
sources.textPlaceholder: Paste here the passage this conversation should be able to consult
sources.textHint: The text is paginated and read on demand, like any other source — pasting it in the chat would keep all of it in context every turn.
sources.siteHint: The page is downloaded and stored as text: a snapshot, so the citation keeps holding even if the site changes.
sources.viewerEmpty: Click a citation in the conversation to open the passage here.
sources.viewerMissing: Source {{id}} is not in this conversation any more — it was removed, or moved to another area. Look for the file in the Sources tab.
sources.truncatedView: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} pages — the document is too large to scroll in one go. Use Original to see the rest.
sources.actionFailed: The action could not be completed.
sources.draftHint: Bring the material before asking: whatever you attach here becomes part of the conversation as soon as you send the first message.
sources.docxUnavailable: This document could not be displayed as it looks. The Text view still shows its content.

appCrash.title: Something went wrong while drawing the screen.
appCrash.hint: The error below is also in the terminal log. Reloading keeps your conversations.

agent.title: Browser tools for the agent
agent.description: The agent opens pages, tests, takes screenshots and documents on its own. When off, it only uses the browser when you open it in fullscreen and ask from the browser's own chat.

links.title: Open links
links.description: Where links clicked in conversations open.

cookies.title: Keep cookies
cookies.description: How long the built-in browser keeps cookies and logins.

clear.title: Clear browsing data
clear.description: Deletes the built-in browser's cookies, logins and cache now.
